replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
Outcome: NO_ACTION. The SGD 33.77 charge stands as it is; the fare breakdown is left at payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

To the rider. Your receipt distance of 26.2 km looked wrong against the 21 km you usually see, and I accept the three artifacts describe the same trip (trip_id TRP-00108, trace starting 07:19:20 matching the trip record). But both ends of this trip changed after booking. You moved the pickup to Punggol MRT yourself (chat 07:11:58, pin amended 07:12:30) and at 07:41:40 you asked to switch the drop from Terminal 1 to Terminal 3, which the record shows was amended at 07:41:52. When the endpoints change, POL-RD-05 requires the deviation test to be re-run against the platform's re-quoted optimal route between the amended points, and that figure is stored on the trip record: amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 km. It is not for me to re-derive it. That re-quote already absorbs the Punggol pickup and the T3 drop. Against 24.60 km, the governing trace distance of 26.17 km is an excess of 1.57 km, or 6.4%. POL-RD-01 sets a single gate: an excess counts as a deviation only if it exceeds 20% of the optimal route (4.92 km here) AND 0.8 km absolute. 6.4% is far below 20%, so no deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 says the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, save for a billing-integrity correction. The 26.2 km on your receipt is the actual distance driven, and a metered fare charges that; the small margin over the best route is exactly the tolerance the threshold exists to leave alone. The 24.8% deviation_pct on the trip record and the 5.17 km / 24.62% excess in the GPS derived block are both computed against the pre-amendment 21.0 km estimate and are superseded by the amendments — they cannot be used. Your $6.15 POL-RD-02 recomputation does not run, because POL-RD-02 applies only once a deviation is established, and none is. Your point that the driver admitted going round the loop twice does not change this: the T3 kerb loop followed your own terminal change, and even taken in full the excess over the amended optimal is about 1.57 km, far short of the gate. On your profile, deviation_claims_60d is 1, so the extra-corroboration add-on in POL-RD-08 is not engaged; that finding makes no difference here because the claim fails on the baseline, not on credibility. Neither alternative fare regime applies: the fare model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null (so not POL-RD-11), and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL (so not POL-RD-12).

To the driver. Your account is borne out by the record. The POL-RD-05 baseline is the amended re-quote (24.60 km / 31.0 min), the trace governs at 26.17 km, and the 1.57 km / 6.4% excess fails the POL-RD-01 establishment gate, so no deviation exists and your route is not penalised. No falsification of the amendment is possible: both amendment timestamps and both stored re-quote fields are present and non-null. Distance driven before the 07:41:52 drop amendment is not counted against you, and the T3 circling is at worst excluded under POL-RD-05 and at best immaterial to the gate either way. The POL-RD-06 profile check clears you: deviation_flags_90d is 0 across completed_trips_90d of 402, no pattern is established, and since no deviation is established there is no MATERIAL finding, so neither the POL-RD-06(b) uplift nor a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. No traffic advisory is invoked (EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0), and nothing is decided on POL-RD-03.

On the money and integrity. The fare reconciles to the cent (3.80 + 19.65 + 9.52 + 0.80 = 33.77), there are no ERP or toll lines, and the airport surcharge of 0.00 is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there (POL-RD-09(4) therefore produces no correction and no referral). No fare line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged. There is no distance shortfall favouring the driver (billed 26.2 km vs trace 26.17 km), so no POL-RD-04 driver compensation is due.

On escalation. The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 206 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, so it triggers none of POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. Trip identifiers match across the three artifacts, timestamps do not disagree by more than 10 minutes or run backwards, and the refund does not exceed SGD 150.00. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The deciding facts are carried by the trip record and the GPS trace, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0; confidence in this ruling is 0.9, above the 0.70 floor.
